title: Nails or pins made by one worker in a day, in Adam Smith's examples (log scale)
description: Bar chart on a logarithmic scale of what one worker made in a day in the examples of The Wealth of Nations (1776), Book I, chapter 1: a common smith who has never made nails, two or three hundred (250, the middle of the range); a smith used to making nails but not a nailer, eight hundred or a thousand (900); boys who have made nothing but nails, upwards of 2,300; and a man's share in a pin workshop of ten, 4,800 pins.
heading: MADE BY ONE WORKER IN A DAY · LOG SCALE
